cita: Anokhin et al. (2024). AriGraph: Learning Knowledge Graph World Models with Episodic Memory for LLM Agents.
problema: Addresses that unstructured memory representations (full history, summarization, vector RAG) fail to support reasoning and planning for complex, partially-observable decision-making tasks, and that current LLM agents lack a way to jointly learn semantic and episodic knowledge from environment interaction.
mecanismo: AriGraph builds an updating memory graph combining semantic vertices/edges (triplets extracted from observations) with episodic vertices/edges (raw observations linked to co-occurring triplets); on each step it WRITEs new triplets, detects and removes outdated edges (ACTUALIZACION/OLVIDO) by comparing them against existing semantic edges, and retrieves via a two-stage semantic-then-episodic graph search (Contriever embeddings + graph traversal) feeding a ReAct planning/decision loop whose working memory holds the evolving sub-goal plan.
evaluacion: Evaluated the Ariadne agent (AriGraph + planning + ReAct decision-making) against full-history, summarization, RAG, RAG+Reflexion and Simulacra baselines plus RL baselines (GATA/LTL-GATA/EXPLORER) on TextWorld tasks (Treasure Hunt, Cleaning, Cooking, 3 difficulty tiers each), on NetHack (vs NetPlay with restricted vs full observations), and zero-shot on multi-hop QA (Musique, HotpotQA, 200 samples each) against GraphReader/ReadAgent/HOLMES/GraphRAG/RAG.
numeros_clave: NetHack Room-Obs: Ariadne score 593.00+/-202.62 / 6.33+/-2.31 levels vs NetPlay(Room obs) 341.67+/-109.14 / 3.67+/-1.15 vs NetPlay(Level obs, oracle) 675.33+/-130.27 / 7.33+/-1.15 (Table 1); AriGraph reported >10x cheaper than GraphRAG on multi-hop QA (Table 3, Appendix D).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Measured two-stage semantic+episodic graph retrieval beats vector RAG/full-history/summarization baselines on TextWorld and multi-hop QA (Fig 3, Table 2), supporting MF's stance of measuring retrieval rather than assuming embeddings suffice.

The outdated-edge detection step (filter semantic edges incident to new triplets, compare, remove stale edges before adding new ones, Sec 2 'Constructing AriGraph') is a concrete write-time staleness-correction mechanism MF could adapt for docs/index drift.
Working memory explicitly stores the evolving sub-goal plan, revised every step from environment feedback (Sec 3), evidencing plan-state as first-class memory (plan_estado=SI).

notes: Numbers from Table 1 (Sec 5.2 NetHack), Fig 3-5, and multi-hop QA Table 2/3 Appendix D — arXiv:2407.04363v3.

cita: Chatterjee and Agarwal (2025). Semantic Anchoring in Agentic Memory: Leveraging Linguistic Structures for Persistent Conversational Context.
problema: Targets the failure of vector-only RAG memory to capture linguistic structure (syntactic dependencies, discourse relations, coreference) needed for accurate multi-session recall, causing failures on paraphrase, ellipsis and implicit cross-session references.
mecanismo: Semantic Anchoring stores each memory entry as a hybrid tuple (utterance, coreference-linked entities, dependency parse, discourse-relation vector, dense embedding) written into a hybrid index (FAISS dense + Whoosh symbolic inverted index); retrieval fuses cosine similarity, entity-match and discourse-match into one weighted score, then serializes the linguistically-tagged memory into the LLM context.
evaluacion: Evaluated on two adapted long-term dialogue datasets (MultiWOZ-Long, DialogRE-L) against Stateless-LLM, Vector-RAG (Sentence-BERT+FAISS) and Entity-RAG baselines, measuring Factual Recall, Discourse Coherence and human-judged User Continuity Satisfaction (5 annotators, Krippendorff's alpha=0.81), plus an ablation removing each linguistic component.
numeros_clave: MultiWOZ-Long: FR 83.5% / DC 80.8% / UCS 4.3 for full model vs Vector-RAG 71.6%/66.4%/3.4 (Table 1); ablation: removing discourse tagging drops FR by 4.7pts, removing coreference drops DC by 6.2pts (Table 3).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Shows a measured hybrid retrieval design (dense + symbolic linguistic index) beating pure vector-RAG (FR 83.5% vs 71.6%, Table 1) - a concrete pattern MF's measured retrieval layer (G-M2) could borrow rather than trusting embeddings alone.

Coreference/discourse tagging is framed as improving interpretability of what was retrieved, not as a provenance/staleness mechanism, so it is only tangentially relevant to MF's anti-drift concerns (Sec 3.5).

notes: Table 1 MultiWOZ-Long, Table 3 ablation, Sec 5.5 human eval (arXiv:2508.12630v1); single-paper synthetic-dataset study, modest evidentiary weight.

cita: Ocker et al. (2025). A Grounded Memory System For Smart Personal Assistants.
problema: Addresses the need for a personal-assistant memory that is grounded in real-world multimodal perception (video) with explicit spatial/temporal structure, since standard RAG stores disconnected snippets that fail to capture relational dependencies needed for complex situational queries.
mecanismo: Three-phase pipeline: (1) perception - a VLM (gpt-4o) captions video frame sequences into agent/object/action-labeled MemoryNotes; (2) WRITE/ingestion - notes become nodes in a Neo4j knowledge graph (image nodes sequentially linked via has-previous, entities linked via has-element) plus dense embeddings (text-embedding-3-small) in a vector store; (3) agentic retrieval combines semantic vector search, PageRank graph expansion, and text2cypher structured queries, exposed as tools an LLM agent selects among.
evaluacion: Demonstrated qualitatively on a single real-world home video recorded on iPhone 15 (3Hz frames, captioned every 5th frame); Table 1 shows representative question-answer pairs (counting, existence, emotional-state, descriptive queries) with all listed answers reported correct - no quantitative benchmark or baseline comparison is run.
numeros_clave: Demo corpus reached 329 images stored in memory at query time (Table 1, 'How many images are there in memory?' -> 329); no ablation or benchmark numbers are reported (evidencia_tipo=CUALITATIVA).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Uses one knowledge-graph+vector hybrid store as the single source of truth per fact (image/agent/object/action nodes all in one Neo4j graph), an example single-source-per-fact pattern relevant to MF's seams anchor (Sec 3.3).

Grounds every memory note in a source image/video frame for traceability, but the paper is a qualitative demo (one video, no error analysis), so provenance strength is illustrated, not measured (Sec 5).

notes: Table 1 (Sec 4 examples), Sec 3.3 ingestion pipeline (arXiv:2505.06328v1); single-video qualitative demo, no baseline comparison.

cita: Sen et al. (2026). Chronos: Temporal-Aware Conversational Agents with Structured Event Retrieval for Long-Term Memory.
problema: Targets the tradeoff in long-term conversational memory between comprehensive knowledge-graph extraction (high overhead, context entropy from irrelevant precomputed facts) and simple turn-level retrieval (lacks temporal grounding for date-sensitive, multi-hop queries).
mecanismo: Chronos WRITEs only temporally-grounded event tuples (subject-verb-object with resolved ISO 8601 datetime ranges plus 2-4 lexical aliases) into an event calendar, alongside raw turns in a separate turn calendar (both embedded via text-embedding-3-large); at query time a per-question 'dynamic prompting' step generates tailored retrieval guidance, an initial dense-search+rerank(Cohere v3)+context-expansion stage seeds the agent, and a ReAct tool-calling agent iteratively searches/greps both calendars before answering.
evaluacion: Evaluated on the LongMemEvalS benchmark (500 questions, 6 categories) with GPT-4o (Chronos Low) and Claude Opus 4.6 (Chronos High) against EmergenceMem, Honcho, Mastra, Zep, Supermemory, Hindsight and full-context baselines, plus an ablation isolating the contribution of the events calendar and other components.
numeros_clave: Chronos Low 92.60% / Chronos High 95.60% overall accuracy on LongMemEvalS vs best prior EmergenceMem 86.00% (+7.67% relative); ablation: events calendar alone accounts for a 58.9% gain over baseline, other components 15.5-22.3% (Abstract, Table 1-2).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Measured, per-component ablation (events calendar = 58.9% of the accuracy gain, Abstract) is exactly the kind of measured-retrieval evidence MF's G-M2 requires before trusting an architecture choice.

Query-conditioned selective extraction (structure only temporal events, keep the rest as raw turns) is a concrete pattern to bound what gets written/indexed and control context/token cost, relevant to MF's context-economy anchor (Sec 1, 'context entropy').

notes: Abstract, Table 1-2 LongMemEvalS results, Sec 3.1/3.5 ablation discussion (arXiv:2603.16862v1).

cita: Zhang et al. (2026). DeltaMem: Towards Agentic Memory Management via Reinforcement Learning.
problema: Targets information loss in multi-agent persona-memory pipelines (separate extraction/retrieval/update stages act as lossy compression across session boundaries) and the lack of operation-level training data/rewards for learning memory-update policies.
mecanismo: DeltaMem is a single ReAct agent that jointly retrieves and updates a persona memory bank per dialogue session, outputting WRITE/ADMISION(add)/ACTUALIZACION(update) operations end-to-end; it is trained via RL using a novel Memory-based Levenshtein Distance reward (optimal-transport alignment between predicted and target memory-state deltas, soft precision/recall/F1) rather than downstream-task accuracy, on a synthesized dataset of dialogues with operation-level labels (profile enrichment -> event generation -> memory generation -> dialogue generation).
evaluacion: Evaluated training-free and RL-trained (Qwen3-4B/8B) DeltaMem against product-level baselines (A-Mem, Mem0, LangMem, Zep, Memobase, Supermemory, Mirix, LightMem, Memory-R1) on three long-term memory benchmarks: LoCoMo, HaluMem (extraction/update/QA), and PersonaMem, plus an ablation on the local lexical fidelity term.
numeros_clave: DeltaMem-8B-RL reaches 66.43 QA score on HaluMem, surpassing the best training-free baseline LightMem and commercial Zep; ablation of local lexical fidelity costs about 3 points on PersonaMem (Sec 5.2, Table 2-3).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Formulates the write/update decision as a single end-to-end agent action (not a separate extraction-then-update pipeline), an alternative discretionary-write pattern MF could weigh against its current write-trigger design (Sec 3.1).

The memory-based Levenshtein/optimal-transport reward gives a reusable measured notion of how wrong a memory update is (soft precision/recall over state deltas) that could inform how MF validates a write against staleness/drift (Sec 3.3.2).

cita: Li, Zhang, Yang, Ma & Guo (2026). Time is Not a Label: Continuous Phase Rotation for Temporal Knowledge Graphs and Agentic Memory.
problema: Targets the 'static-dynamic dilemma' in graph-based agentic memory: discrete timestamp metadata cannot distinguish permanent facts (e.g. 'born in') from evolving ones (e.g. 'president of'), forcing systems to choose between destructive overwriting, expensive per-ingestion LLM arbitration, or recency sorting that buries old-yet-permanent knowledge.
mecanismo: RoMem is an append-only, drop-in temporal re-ranker for graph memory: entities/relations are embedded as complex vectors rotated by a per-relation phase angle whose speed alpha_r in (0,1) is predicted zero-shot from the relation's text embedding via a pretrained Semantic Speed Gate (static relations rotate near 0, dynamic ones rotate fast); at retrieval, obsolete facts are geometrically 'shadowed' (rotated out of phase) by fresher ones without deletion, and the temporal score multiplicatively re-ranks HippoRAG's dense+PageRank semantic score.
evaluacion: Evaluated on temporal knowledge-graph completion (ICEWS05-15, MRR/Hit@k vs DistMult/ChronoR/TeRo/TimeGate/etc.) and, applied to agentic memory, on a three-tier benchmark spectrum: heavy-temporal MultiTQ, hybrid LoCoMo, and static DMR-MSC, plus zero-shot FinTMMBench, against Mem0/Zep/LicoMemory/HippoRAG/A-Mem baselines.
numeros_clave: RoMem-ChronoR reaches 72.6 MRR on ICEWS05-15 (SOTA, vs ChronoR backbone 68.4); on MultiTQ raises HippoRAG's MRR from 0.203 to 0.337 and LLM@5 accuracy from 0.112 to 0.366 (2-3x); on static DMR-MSC preserves MRR 0.856 vs HippoRAG 0.848 (near-zero degradation) (Table 1-2, Sec 4.2-4.3).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Offers an append-only, geometric alternative to destructive overwriting or per-ingestion LLM arbitration for resolving conflicting/stale facts (obsolete facts rotated out of phase, not deleted), directly relevant to MF's staleness/poisoning anchor (Sec 3.6).

Measured, per-benchmark ablation showing the temporal re-ranker triples downstream QA accuracy on MultiTQ (0.112 to 0.366) while leaving static retrieval unchanged (DMR-MSC), the kind of measured retrieval evidence G-M2 asks for before adopting a mechanism.
